# Glossary {.unnumbered}

Short definitions of the terms this book uses. Where a chapter treats a term in depth, it is named. Aimed at readers new to research; skip what you already know.

Alt text
:   The text description of a figure that a screen reader speaks aloud. Write it to convey the chart type, the axes, and the finding, not merely the title ([colour and accessibility](14-colour.qmd)).

APC (article processing charge)
:   The fee an open-access journal charges the author to publish. Can run to several thousand euros; many funders and institutions cover it.

Association vs causation
:   An association is a statistical relationship between two variables; a causal effect is one changing the other. Observational data show association; only randomisation or an explicit causal design licenses causal language ([statistical writing](statistical-writing.qmd)).

AUC / c-statistic
:   Area under the ROC curve, and the equivalent concordance statistic: a model's ability to rank a patient with the event above one without it. 0.5 is chance, 1.0 is perfect ([prediction models](prediction-models.qmd)).

Bootstrap
:   Resampling the data with replacement to estimate uncertainty or to correct a model's optimism. A way to get a confidence interval or an internal-validation estimate without a formula.

Calibration
:   The agreement between a model's predicted probabilities and observed frequencies — whether "20% risk" happens to one in five. Distinct from discrimination and more often omitted ([prediction models](prediction-models.qmd)).

Colour-vision deficiency (CVD)
:   Reduced ability to distinguish certain hues; the red–green types affect about 8% of men, so a figure must never carry meaning by colour alone ([colour and accessibility](14-colour.qmd)).

Confidence interval (CI)
:   The range of values compatible with the data at a stated level (usually 95%). Report it with every estimate; it carries the uncertainty a p-value hides.

Confounding
:   A third variable associated with both exposure and outcome that distorts their apparent relationship. Adjusted for by design (randomisation) or in analysis (regression), never fully in observational data.

CONSORT
:   The reporting guideline for randomised controlled trials, including the flow diagram of participants ([reporting](06-reporting-guidelines.qmd)).

CRediT
:   The Contributor Roles Taxonomy: fourteen standard roles (conceptualisation, analysis, writing, etc.) used to state who did what ([co-authorship](08-co-authorship.qmd)).

Cross-validation
:   Repeatedly splitting data into training and testing folds to estimate how a model performs on unseen data. Internal validation; weaker than external validation.

Data-to-ink ratio
:   Tufte's principle that a figure should spend its ink on data and erase decoration that carries no information ([principles of data visualisation](10-principles.qmd)).

Decision-curve analysis (DCA)
:   A plot of a model's net benefit against the "treat all" and "treat none" strategies across decision thresholds — whether acting on the model beats the blunt alternatives ([prediction models](prediction-models.qmd)).

De-identification
:   Removing direct and indirect identifiers so data can be shared without exposing individuals (e.g. HIPAA Safe Harbor, k-anonymity) ([reproducibility](reproducibility.qmd)).

Discrimination
:   A model's ability to separate those who have the outcome from those who do not, summarised by the AUC/c-statistic.

DOI (digital object identifier)
:   A permanent identifier for a paper, dataset, or software release. A Zenodo or Dryad deposit issues one so the object stays citable and findable.

EQUATOR Network
:   The online library cataloguing every published reporting guideline ([reporting](06-reporting-guidelines.qmd)).

External validation
:   Testing a model on data from a different setting, time, or population than it was built on — the evidence that it transports.

FAIR
:   Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable: the principles for research-data management, mostly a matter of good metadata ([reproducibility](reproducibility.qmd)).

False-discovery rate (FDR)
:   The expected proportion of false positives among the results called significant; controlled by the Benjamini–Hochberg procedure when many tests are run.

Forest plot
:   A plot of effect estimates, one row per study or subgroup, each with its confidence interval, and in meta-analysis a pooled diamond at the foot ([systematic reviews](systematic-reviews.qmd); [chart types](11-chart-types.qmd)).

Hazard ratio (HR)
:   The ratio of event rates between groups at any instant, from a survival (time-to-event) analysis. HR 1.3 means a 30% higher instantaneous risk.

Hedging
:   Calibrating the strength of a claim to the strength of the evidence — neither overstating nor burying a finding ([clear writing](03-clear-writing.qmd)).

ICMJE
:   The International Committee of Medical Journal Editors, whose recommendations define authorship, trial registration, and disclosure norms.

Impact factor
:   The average citations per article for a journal over two years. A crude, gamed proxy for quality; useful only as one weak signal among many.

IMRAD
:   The Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion structure of a scientific article ([article structure](02-article-structure.qmd)).

Intention-to-treat (ITT)
:   Analysing trial participants in the arm they were randomised to, regardless of what they received. Preserves randomisation; contrast with per-protocol.

Interquartile range (IQR)
:   The 25th-to-75th-percentile span of a distribution; the spread to report with a median for skewed data.

Kaplan–Meier curve
:   A step plot of the probability of remaining event-free over time, estimated so that censored participants still contribute until they leave ([chart types](11-chart-types.qmd)).

Missingness (MCAR / MAR / MNAR)
:   Missing Completely At Random, At Random (given observed data), or Not At Random. The mechanism decides which handling is valid.

Multiple imputation (MICE)
:   A method for handling missing data by creating several completed datasets, analysing each, and pooling — Multiple Imputation by Chained Equations ([statistical writing](statistical-writing.qmd)).

Multiplicity
:   The inflation of false positives when many hypotheses are tested; addressed by correction (Bonferroni, FDR) ([statistical writing](statistical-writing.qmd)).

Net benefit
:   The decision-curve metric that weighs true positives against false positives at a given decision threshold.

Odds ratio (OR)
:   The ratio of the odds of an outcome between groups, from logistic regression. Approximates the risk ratio only when the outcome is rare.

Okabe-Ito
:   An eight-colour categorical palette chosen to stay distinguishable under the common types of colour-vision deficiency; the categorical scale used for the treatment arms in this book ([colour and accessibility](14-colour.qmd)).

Open access
:   Publication free for readers, funded by an APC (gold) or by self-archiving (green).

Overfitting
:   A model that fits its training data too closely and fails on new data; visible as a calibration slope below 1 ([prediction models](prediction-models.qmd)).

Palette (categorical, sequential, diverging)
:   A set of colours chosen by the data it encodes: categorical for unordered groups, sequential for ordered magnitude (one luminance direction), diverging for values either side of a meaningful midpoint ([colour and accessibility](14-colour.qmd)).

Peer review
:   Evaluation of a manuscript by independent experts before publication; single- or double-blind depending on what is concealed ([editorial process](05-editorial-process.qmd)).

Per-protocol
:   Analysing only participants who completed the intervention as assigned. Answers a different question from ITT and can reintroduce selection bias.

PPI (patient and public involvement)
:   Patients or the public shaping the question, design, or dissemination of research; reported against GRIPP2 ([reporting](06-reporting-guidelines.qmd)).

Predatory journal
:   A journal that charges an APC but provides no genuine peer review or editorial service ([editorial process](05-editorial-process.qmd)).

Preprint
:   A manuscript posted publicly (e.g. medRxiv) before peer review, to share results early and establish priority.

Preregistration
:   Recording the hypothesis and analysis plan in a public registry before data collection, to separate confirmatory from exploratory analysis ([open science](open-science.qmd)).

PRISMA
:   The reporting guideline for systematic reviews and meta-analyses, including the flow diagram ([systematic reviews](systematic-reviews.qmd)).

Prospective / retrospective
:   Whether data are collected forward from a defined start (prospective) or assembled from records after the fact (retrospective).

PROSPERO
:   The international registry for systematic-review protocols.

P-value
:   The probability of data at least as extreme as observed, if the null hypothesis were true. Not the probability the null is true; report it beside an effect estimate, never alone.

Random seed
:   A fixed starting value that makes a random procedure repeatable, so an analysis returns the same numbers each run ([reproducibility](reproducibility.qmd)).

renv / requirements.txt
:   Files that pin the exact package versions a project used, so its computational environment can be rebuilt.

Reporting guideline
:   A checklist specifying what a given study design must report (CONSORT, STROBE, PRISMA, TRIPOD…) ([reporting](06-reporting-guidelines.qmd)).

Reproducibility
:   The property that another researcher with your data and code can rerun the analysis and get the same results ([reproducibility](reproducibility.qmd)).

Risk ratio (relative risk, RR)
:   The ratio of outcome probabilities between groups. More directly interpretable than an odds ratio.

ROC curve
:   Receiver operating characteristic: sensitivity plotted against 1 − specificity across thresholds; its area is the AUC.

Sensitivity / specificity
:   The proportion of true positives correctly identified (sensitivity) and true negatives correctly excluded (specificity) by a test at a threshold.

Sensitivity analysis
:   Repeating the primary analysis under different assumptions to test how robust the finding is ([statistical writing](statistical-writing.qmd)). (Distinct from the diagnostic term *sensitivity*.)

Small multiples
:   A grid of small panels that share axes and scale, one per group, so the eye compares by position instead of untangling overlaid series ([pitfalls](12-pitfalls.qmd)).

SPIRIT
:   The reporting guideline for clinical-trial protocols.

STROBE
:   The reporting guideline for observational studies (cohort, case-control, cross-sectional).

Systematic review / meta-analysis
:   A structured synthesis of all studies on a question (systematic review) and their statistical pooling (meta-analysis) ([systematic reviews](systematic-reviews.qmd)).

TRIPOD+AI
:   The reporting guideline for clinical prediction models, including machine-learning models ([prediction models](prediction-models.qmd)).

viridis
:   A perceptually uniform sequential colourmap that stays legible in greyscale and under colour-vision deficiency ([colour and accessibility](14-colour.qmd)).

Zenodo
:   A CERN-hosted repository that issues a citable DOI for datasets and software releases and archives GitHub repositories ([open science](open-science.qmd)).
